 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 27.10.2017 at about 10.30 a.m. the petitioner was a pillion rider in a motor cycle baring No.KA-01-HW-5076 along with rider C.N.Sagar and were proceeding from Hosa road towards K.R.Puram on Haralur road, at that time the driver of the three wheeler goods van bearing No.KA-02-AE-7870 came from behind with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Sakra Hospital, wherein he took the first aid treatment, later on he was shifted to St.John's hospital and again he was shifted to M.G. Speciality hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 44 years, working as a plumber under one Dinesh, Plumbing works contractor,
Somasundarpalya, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556.

Therefore,
the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

Contending the above facts,
he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, placed exparte.
The respondent No2 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement.

5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further this respondent has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.
KA-02-AE- 7870 and its validity.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S.
134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
Further contended that the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.

Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.
6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the three wheeler goods van bearing registration No.KA-02-AE-7870 on 27.10.2017 at about 10.30 a.m. infront of Spring field apartment, Haraluru junction, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has not led any evidence on its behalf.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.

14. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of his evidence, he has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P6 such as FIR with complaint,
Spot mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
15. On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by Sagar, Son of Nagaraju on 27.10.2017.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by HSR Layout Traffic Police in Cr. No.119/2017 against the driver of the three wheeler goods van bearing No.KA-02-AE-7870 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC and S.134(A & B) R/w S. 187 of IMV Act.
On perusal of Ex.P2 andEx.P3 are the spot mahazar and sketch also reveals the scene of occurrence and it corroborate the evidence of PW1.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report reveals that the damages caused to the vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AE-7870 and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex. P5 is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P65 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the three wheeler goods van for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC and S.134(A & B), S.56 and S.192 of IMV Act.
16. The respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle and not on the part of the driver of the three wheeler goods van.
To substantiate the said fact, the respondent No.2 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
Moreover he has not challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the three wheeler goods van.
On the other hand, petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

22. Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.

23. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 44 years, plumber under one Dinesh plumbing works contractor, Somasundarapalya, Bengaluru and getting an income of Rs.18,000/- per month.
But he has not produced pertains to his avocation and income.
In the absence of the documents pertains to his avocation and income, it is very difficult to assess the income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner and the year of accident, if notional income of Rs.7,000/- per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P7, which shows that he was admitted from 27.10.2017 and discharged from 31.10.2017.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries; he might have taken rest and treatment at least for two months.
Therefore, two months income comes to Rs.14,000/- is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
24. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
On record he has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P10 to the extent of Rs.1,39,038 /- and advance bills marked at Ex.P11 and prescriptions marked at Ex.P13.
On perusal of medical bills produced by the petitioner expenses charged by the hospital is very high.
On perusal of discharge summary marked at Ex.P7, underwent wound operation and wound debridement and sutured in layers.
Even the petitioner has not examined the doctor to show that for his injuries he has spent Rs.1,39,038/-.
Any how considering the nature of the injuries, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses.
25. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 44 years, plumber and getting an income of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Due to the accident he is unable to attend the duty and not getting his income.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability.
The petitioner has produced Lab report, marked at Ex.P8, CT can report at Ex.P9.
Therefore, no amount is granted under this head.
26. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained fractures.
So his happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out his life.
Hence, it is just and necessary to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of amenities.
27. PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident he took the treatment as inpatient.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of attendant, conveyance,
food and nourishment etc.

28. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
 Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs. 30,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 14,000-00 and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 50,000-00 4. Loss of future income Nil 5. Loss of amenities, Rs. 20,000-00 6. Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 15,000-00 conveyance charges Total Rs.1,29,000-00 29.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the three wheeler van bearing No.KA-02-AE-7870.
30.
The respondent No.2 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect o three wheeler van bearing No.KA-02-AE- 7870 and its validity.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
31.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,29,000/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
